mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 1% per month for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases uncertainty and reduces risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are above their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between HOUST (housing starts) and GDPC1 over the past six months indicates robust housing demand coinciding with overall economic expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Pearson correlation(HOUST, GDPC1) > 0.7 over last 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST and GDPC1 are strongly positively correlated over the prior six months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 100,000 for four consecutive months signals robust labor market strength, which supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by at least 100,000 for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 10-year average, combined with a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate, indicates households are drawing down savings to sustain consumption, which temporarily supports equities but ultimately increases default risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY change < 10-year RSAFS average AND UNRATE rising
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS falls below its 10-year average and UNRATE is rising.
